target: ADR-001 Executable validation for Dart API contracts

decisions.question: Materialize ADR-001 as accepted, or as proposed with the Decision left as a TODO?

options.label: accepted
options.consequence: binding at once; hsdd-config injects its Decision and Consequences into every phase context that touches a contract, and the nine contract steps author fixtures in its format

options.label: proposed with TODO
options.consequence: hsdd-adr's rule for a decision the human has not stated; every contract step would lack a binding fixture format

decisions.why: The owner's decision policy accepts every proposed ADR, and the decision content is not invented: it is the root decomposition's proposal plus the sharpenings recorded below, each with evidence from docs/auto-run/experiments/contract-fixtures/.

decisions.question: Filename slug and title of ADR-001.

options.label: 001-executable-contract-validation, root title kept
options.consequence: the slug names the topic, which covers all five kinds; the title matches the root's heading, OQ8 and every citation

options.label: 001-dart-api-contract-validation
options.consequence: mirrors the title but understates the schema, file and cli items

options.label: retitle to Executable contract validation
options.consequence: more accurate, but the root heading and OQ8 detail would read differently from the file

decisions.why: hsdd-adr asks for a 2 to 4 word topic slug; the topic is executable validation of every contract kind, while the title keeps the id and wording the root already uses. No evidence beyond naming consistency.

decisions.question: Fixtures live under hsdd/ at the workspace root, belong to the root package, and reject fixtures hold deliberate errors. How are they kept out of workspace-wide analysis, and which analysis options apply to them?

options.label: root excludes hsdd/**, fixture-local options with no lints and strict modes
options.consequence: workspace-wide fvm dart analyze never sees a fixture; the replay tool analyzes explicit paths under hsdd/contract/fixture/analysis_options.yaml, which drops the root lint set and turns on strict-casts, strict-inference, strict-raw-types; ADR-002's root options gain one exclude

options.label: root lints apply, root dev-depends on members
options.consequence: depend_on_referenced_packages silenced by dependencies, but a workspace-wide analyze still fails on every reject fixture and on bindings whose producer is absent, so an exclude is needed anyway; fixture verdicts then depend on whatever lint set the root adopts

options.label: replay copies fixtures into a temporary package
options.consequence: isolation, but the copy sits outside the workspace and loses its package resolution

decisions.chosen: root excludes hsdd/**, fixture-local options with no lints and strict modes
decisions.why: The experiment shows the exclude hides fixtures from a workspace-wide analyze while an explicit path is still analyzed, and that a nested analysis_options.yaml replaces the root lint set (without it depend_on_referenced_packages fires on every import). Strict modes make a surface fixture fail on raw types and inference failures, which catches signatures that leak dynamic into consumer code; a lint set would make fixture verdicts depend on style rules unrelated to the contract.

decisions.question: How does a reject fixture name its expected diagnostic, and when does it pass?

options.label: line-anchored marker, exact match at every severity
options.consequence: a `// expect-diagnostic: {code}` comment on its own line expects {code} (lowercase, as --format=json reports it) on the next line, like `// ignore:`; the file passes when reported (line, code) pairs at every severity equal the marked pairs; catches wrong lines, extra diagnostics and wrong codes, and pins warning-severity guarantees such as @visibleForTesting

options.label: file-level header, errors only (root proposal)
options.consequence: simpler to write, but passes a marker on the wrong line and a misuse that fails for another reason in the same file, and cannot pin a warning-severity guarantee

options.label: Dart SDK static-error test markers with columns
options.consequence: column-precise, but verbose and tied to SDK test tooling that is not a pub package

decisions.chosen: line-anchored marker, exact match at every severity
decisions.why: The prototype in the experiment passes the good set and fails the three broken cases (wrong line, extra diagnostics, a plausible but wrong code authored without running the analyzer), all of which a file-level, errors-only match lets through in part. JSON output gives the lowercase code and 1-based line directly. If fixtures turned out to need column precision (two misuses on one line), the SDK marker format would win.

decisions.question: What shape does a behavior fixture take so one suite validates implementations that need different test runners (VM and widget tree)?

options.label: cases as values plus per-implementation bindings
options.consequence: a conformance library declares a harness interface (factories plus settle()) and exports List<ConformanceCase<H>>, a record ({String name, Future<void> Function(H) body}) shared through package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart; it asserts with package:matcher/expect.dart and imports no test runner; each binding registers the cases with test or testWidgets

options.label: suite registers its own tests (root proposal wording)
options.consequence: a function taking factories that calls test() itself; cannot obtain a WidgetTester, so a Flutter implementation needs a second suite that drifts

options.label: one suite per runner
options.consequence: no shared abstraction, two copies of every guarantee

decisions.chosen: cases as values plus per-implementation bindings
decisions.why: The experiment binds one conformance library under test on the VM and under testWidgets with pumpAndSettle, from the same file. Cases as values keep the suite pure data and the binding a thin shell, which is the owner's functional-first preference. The shared record alias lives in the replay tool's library so every suite uses one shape; a per-suite inline typedef would also work structurally and was the close alternative.

decisions.question: Where do bindings live, who writes them, how are they named, and how are they bound before the producing package exists?

options.label: in the fixture directory of the contract that declares the implementation, written by hsdd-contract
options.consequence: behavior/{implementation}_test.dart next to the suite, or importing another contract's suite by relative path (bus-api@v1 binds topology-dsl@v1's live builder; flutter-binding@v1 binds navigation-api@v1's executor); every contract step writes only its own directory; the producer's gate exercises the bound suite; bindings are forward references until the producer's first phase lands; the Validation section lists each binding

options.label: in each implementing package's test/, written by its phases
options.consequence: bindings compile from day one of the package, but a phase could bind a subset of cases and HSDD keeps fixtures out of phase hands

options.label: in the suite's own directory for every implementation
options.consequence: one place per suite, but the navigation-api@v1 step would write a binding against flutter-binding@v1's surface before that contract exists

decisions.chosen: in the fixture directory of the contract that declares the implementation, written by hsdd-contract
decisions.why: hsdd-contract: 'Authoring writes the artifact' and 'A phase never writes them'. Placing a binding with the contract that declares the implementation means the producer of that contract replays it with no cross-node selection, and the producer-first order of the contract steps (execution plan S06..S14) already writes each suite before its foreign bindings. A consumer's stand-in, which no contract declares, is the one binding a phase writes, in its own test/ directory by relative import (Q15).

decisions.question: What does the replay do with a binding whose implementing package does not exist yet?

options.label: fail, reported as PENDING
options.consequence: a mis-scheduled gate cannot pass; the message tells an absent producer apart from a failing case; nidana.integration's --all run fails until every producer exists

options.label: skip with a warning
options.consequence: early gates stay green, but a renamed or missing package passes a gate silently

options.label: author bindings only once the package exists
options.consequence: no pending state, but every contract needs a second hsdd-contract pass after its producer's first phase

decisions.why: Under the binding-location rule, a binding is only pending when a replay runs before its own producer's first phase, which no gate should do; failing keeps that visible. The workspace package configuration identifies the absent package before running (Q14). Had bindings been placed in the suite's directory for foreign implementations, skipping would have been needed and the decision would flip.

decisions.question: How does the replay choose the test runner for a binding, and from which directory does it run?

options.label: by import, from the workspace root, pinned SDK
options.consequence: a binding importing package:flutter_test runs under flutter test --no-pub, any other under dart test, both from the root; flutter is derived from the dart running the tool, so both use the fvm pin

options.label: a runner header in each binding
options.consequence: explicit, but a header can disagree with the imports

options.label: run each binding from its implementing package's directory
options.consequence: matches Flutter habits, but the tool must map bindings to packages and the root already works

decisions.chosen: by import, from the workspace root, pinned SDK
decisions.why: flutter test --no-pub runs a binding under hsdd/ from the pure-Dart workspace root, and dart test cannot load it, so the runner must be chosen per binding; the import cannot lie. The tool's Platform.resolvedExecutable is the fvm-pinned SDK's dart inside the Flutter SDK, so the matching flutter is derivable.

decisions.question: How is the replay tool invoked from a gate?

options.label: one CLI: fvm dart run nidana_contract_check {slug}... [--set] [--guarantee] or --all
options.consequence: one command per gate line; sets structure, surface, reject, behavior, schema, file, cli; structure always runs first and needs no implementation; one line per fixture, non-zero exit on any failure

options.label: a script per set
options.consequence: simpler tool, longer and drift-prone gate lines

options.label: a package:test meta-suite
options.consequence: familiar output, but analysis and recorded invocations fit awkwardly in test cases

decisions.chosen: one CLI: fvm dart run nidana_contract_check {slug}... [--set] [--guarantee] or --all
decisions.why: dart run {member} works from the workspace root without the root depending on the member, so the gate line is short and needs no path. A --binding selector was considered and dropped: with bindings placed by declaring contract, every binding in a slug's directory belongs to that slug's producer.

decisions.question: Which fixture sets does an intermediate producing phase's gate run, when later phases deliver the remaining behavior?

options.label: type-level sets in full, behavior restricted cumulatively, unrestricted at the last producing phase
options.consequence: phase 1 (the skeleton under fp-progression) already passes surface and reject; each later gate names the guarantee ids delivered so far; the last phase producing the contract runs everything

options.label: every set in full at every phase
options.consequence: gates fail until the last phase, so they stop meaning anything

options.label: behavior only at the last phase
options.consequence: simple, but behavior regressions surface late

decisions.chosen: type-level sets in full, behavior restricted cumulatively, unrestricted at the last producing phase
decisions.why: fp-progression makes phase 1 land every declaration of every contract the node produces (conventions), so surface and reject can pass from the first gate, while behavior lands phase by phase. A test-name prefix filter selects cases under both runners (Q9, Q11). This assumes one leaf-parent lands all of a contract's declarations; see notes for nidana.runtime's decomposition.

decisions.question: What must an api or shared-model fixture set minimally contain to count as the executable validation artifact at hsdd-reconcile's draft to stable flip, given that reconcile itself only checks that the path exists?

options.label: guarantee ids with full coverage
options.consequence: every guarantee bullet begins `- **G{n}**`, stable per slug; each is covered by a reject fixture (`// covers: G{n}`) or a behavior case named 'G{n} ...', or listed as `not executable` with the node gate that checks it; surface/ uses the whole Interface; bindings listed in Validation exist; the structure set checks this once the tool exists, reading does until then

options.label: existence only (HSDD default)
options.consequence: one placeholder file satisfies stable; the root's success criterion that every Spec §3 guarantee is covered becomes uncheckable

options.label: a coverage matrix in the Validation section
options.consequence: readable in one place, but a second source of truth beside the fixture headers that drifts

decisions.why: The root's success criteria require every Bus Runtime Contract guarantee to be covered by a contract fixture or a node test a gate runs; ids make that mechanically checkable, and the coverage relation lives in the fixtures themselves. hsdd-config injects the Guarantees section verbatim, so phase contexts carry the ids that gates cite in --guarantee. No runtime evidence; this is a format choice the decision policy assigns to this step.

decisions.question: Which schema dialect and validator, and how does the producer's gate check its real output against the schema?

options.label: draft 2020-12 via package:json_schema; producer side as behavior cases
options.consequence: the schema set checks valid/ validates and invalid/ does not, with no producer; the round trip of every valid/ file and the schema check of real output are cases in the contract's conformance library, through expectMatchesSchema in package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart; json_schema joins the workspace resolution

options.label: draft-07
options.consequence: wider tool support, no unevaluatedProperties, so closed objects composed from $defs cannot be stated

options.label: an emitter command named in Validation
options.consequence: the tool validates a command's stdout; one more protocol to keep beside the behavior bindings

decisions.chosen: draft 2020-12 via package:json_schema; producer side as behavior cases
decisions.why: json_schema 5.2.2 validates $defs, prefixItems, items: false and unevaluatedProperties under draft 2020-12 and resolves alongside Flutter and test in one workspace. Putting the producer-side check in the conformance library reuses the binding mechanism instead of adding a second one.

decisions.question: What exact protocol do file and cli replays follow?

options.label: generator command with placeholders; invocation directories with path normalization
options.consequence: file: Validation names a command with {input} and {output}, run into an empty directory, generated Dart formatted, compared byte for byte with expected/; cli: invocation/{case}/ with args, optional files/ as working directory, exit_code, optional stdout and stderr compared after {files} and {root} substitution; a plugin case enables nidana_dart_lint in files/analysis_options.yaml by relative path; topic-codegen must expose a command entry outside build_runner

options.label: bindings for file and cli too
options.consequence: one mechanism, but every recorded invocation becomes Dart test code and the recorded outputs stop being plain files a reviewer reads

decisions.chosen: generator command with placeholders; invocation directories with path normalization
decisions.why: Plain recorded files are what HSDD's per-kind table asks for (a sample tree, recorded invocations). The experiment shows an input tree under hsdd/ enabling an analysis server plugin by relative path, also when the plugin is a workspace member, and that JSON and machine output carry absolute paths, hence the normalization.

experiments.question: On the pinned SDK, in a workspace laid out like the planned tree (lint-enabled root, pure producer, Flutter implementer, tool stand-in, plugin member, fixtures under hsdd/contract/), how do analysis exclusion, nested analysis options, diagnostic reporting, conformance binding under dart test and flutter test, absent-package bindings, JSON Schema 2020-12 validation, member invocation from the root and plugin-enabled recorded invocations behave?
experiments.finding: Root exclude of hsdd/** hides fixtures from workspace-wide analyze while explicit paths are still analyzed; a nested hsdd/contract/fixture/analysis_options.yaml replaces the root lint set. --format=json gives lowercase codes and 1-based lines at every severity; a line-anchored marker prototype passes the good set and fails wrong-line, extra-diagnostic and wrong-code fixtures (the plausible final_class_extended_outside_of_library is really invalid_use_of_type_outside_library). One value-based conformance library binds under test and under testWidgets; flutter test --no-pub runs it from the pure-Dart root; dart test cannot. Absent-package bindings fail to load and are detectable from package_config. json_schema 5.2.2 handles draft 2020-12. dart run {member} works from the root. An input tree enables an analysis server plugin by relative path, including a workspace-member plugin.

notes_for_orchestrator: Gate: the single error is docs/auto-run/execution-plan.md, modified by the orchestrator before or during this step (S03 row 'running'); commit it separately or rerun the gate after staging it apart.

Contract steps S06..S14, format to follow (ADR-001 Decision items 2 to 8): fixtures under hsdd/contract/fixture/{slug}/; every guarantee bullet starts `- **G{n}** `, ids stable per slug; `## Validation` names the fixture directory, lists each binding as `behavior/{implementation}_test.dart` binds `{subject}_conformance.dart` to {implementation}, lists `- not executable: G{n}, {reason}; checked by {node}'s gates` for anything no fixture can cover, and for serialized forms the schema path.

The first contract step (topic-model@v1) must also write hsdd/contract/fixture/analysis_options.yaml with exactly: analyzer: language: strict-casts: true, strict-inference: true, strict-raw-types: true; no include and no linter rules (copy from docs/auto-run/experiments/contract-fixtures/hsdd/contract/fixture/analysis_options.yaml, dropping its comment if preferred).

surface/: Dart libraries that use every Interface declaration with the stated types written out (e.g. `final String name = topic.name;`), clean under --fatal-infos with strict modes, so no raw generics and no deprecated members.

reject/: one file per type-level guarantee; header `// covers: G{n}`; `// expect-diagnostic: {code}` alone on the line directly above the offending line; lowercase codes as --format=json reports; any other diagnostic in the file, even unused_local_variable, fails it, so write the minimum code. Codes observed on the pinned SDK: undefined_getter, undefined_method, invalid_use_of_type_outside_library (extending a final class outside its library), invalid_use_of_visible_for_testing_member (warning). A guessed code is a likely failure (Q7); a step can confirm codes with a throwaway probe under docs/auto-run/experiments/.

behavior/{subject}_conformance.dart: declare a harness interface (factories plus `Future<void> settle()`), export `List<ConformanceCase<H>>` with string-literal names starting 'G{n} ', import package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart (ConformanceCase, expectMatchesSchema) and package:matcher/expect.dart, never package:test or package:flutter_test. Bindings register with test, or testWidgets when the implementation needs the widget tree.

Binding placement: a binding lives with the contract whose Interface declares the implementation. bus-api@v1 carries the binding of topology-dsl@v1's suite to the runtime's live builder; flutter-binding@v1 carries the binding of navigation-api@v1's executor suite to FlutterNavigationExecutor (testWidgets); topology-dsl@v1 carries its recording-builder binding; navigation-api@v1 binds any in-memory executor its own Interface declares. The producer-first order of S06..S14 already writes each suite before its foreign bindings.

topology-ir@v1: schema at hsdd/contract/schema/topology-ir.schema.json (draft 2020-12), valid/ and invalid/ under its fixture directory, plus round-trip and expectMatchesSchema cases in its conformance library.

topic-codegen@v1 (file): input/ and expected/ trees; Validation names a generator command with {input} and {output}. This obliges nidana_dart_codegen to expose a command entry that runs its builders outside build_runner; settle that in the contract's Interface.

nidana-checks@v1 (cli): invocation/{case}/ with args (first line the command: dart, flutter or {package}:{executable}), optional files/ (working directory), exit_code, optional stdout and stderr compared after {files} and {root} substitution. Enable the plugin in files/analysis_options.yaml with `plugins: nidana_dart_lint: path:` relative to that file (from hsdd/contract/fixture/nidana-checks/invocation/{case}/files/ the path is ../../../../../../packages/nidana_dart_lint). Prefer --format=machine for stable stdout; plugin INFO diagnostics leave exit 0 unless --fatal-infos.
Every contract file adds `Governed by: [ADR-001]`; the minimum content of Decision item 12 is what hsdd-reconcile should check at the draft to stable flip, by reading until the replay tool exists.

S04 (ADR-002) consistency: item 1's root analysis_options.yaml excludes must add hsdd/** (ADR-001 item 2 and Consequences); item 2's nidana_contract_check gains package:json_schema (5.2.2 resolves with Flutter, test and the analyzer plugin deps, Q16); an analysis server plugin that is a workspace member (resolution: workspace) loads when enabled by relative path (Q19), which supports nidana_dart_lint as a member.

nidana.model phase planning: ADR-001 puts the replay tool and package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart in the node's first phase beside the type-level skeleton of three contracts; that may exceed one PE. If the plan splits them, it must order the tool so the skeleton phase's gate can replay. nidana.model.md's isolation line names only surface, reject and schema replays; under ADR-001 its gates also run its own behavior bindings (recording builder, lineage functions). Not a conflict, but worth widening at the node's next spec touch.

nidana.runtime decomposition: Decision item 10 assumes the first phase of the producing leaf-parent lands every declaration of a contract. Keep each of bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1 within one leaf-parent child, or that hsdd-spec step must record how surface and reject replays split.

nidana.navigation.md says the conformance suite is bound by 'every platform executor'; under ADR-001 the Flutter binding is written by hsdd-contract in flutter-binding@v1's fixture directory. Consistent in substance; reword at the next touch if desired.
